title: "What is the minimum trimmed sink rate when bounded below the section stall angle?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
ENTRY_CEILING = 90.0   # s for this render, granted by the user
SOLVE_BUDGET = 15.0     # s for any one solve
PROBE_POOL = 200.0        # s granted for the probe
PROBE_SPENT = 47.4      # s the probe actually used

stall_angle = 6.7
unbounded_sink = 0.56  # from 2026-09-29-01-does-freeing-the-wing-planform-lower-the-trimmed-sink-rate-below-0-84.qmd

sink_rate, opt_plane = optimize_geometry_for_sink_rate(get_airplane, alpha_max=stall_angle)

v_trim = opt_plane.v_trim
sweep = opt_plane.le_sweep
inc = opt_plane.wing_inc
```

::: {.hero}
[`{python} f"{sink_rate:.2f} m/s"`]{.hero-value}
[trimmed sink rate]{.hero-label}
:::

**Answer.** Constraining the trim angle of attack to the section stall limit of [`{python} f"{stall_angle:.1f}°"`]{.key} results in a minimum trimmed sink rate of [`{python} f"{sink_rate:.2f} m/s"`]{.key} at [`{python} f"{v_trim:.2f} m/s"`]{.key}. Compared to the [`{python} f"{unbounded_sink:.2f} m/s"`]{.key} achieved by the [unbounded planform optimization](2026-09-29-01-does-freeing-the-wing-planform-lower-the-trimmed-sink-rate-below-0-84.qmd), the stall constraint raises the sink rate but remains a substantial improvement over the fixed planform. The bounded optimal planform selects a sweep of [`{python} f"{sweep:.1f}°"`]{.key} and wing incidence of [`{python} f"{inc:.1f}°"`]{.key} (@fig-stall-bounded-planform).
